title: Depth and generic restriction for invertible modules on flat reduced curve families
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat finite-type morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose its special fibre $X_k=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$ is reduced and of pure dimension one [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then $X$ is Noetherian (it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]). For every $m\in\mathbf N$, multiplication by $\pi$ on every stalk of $M^{\otimes m}$ is injective, and the restriction map $$H^0(X,M^{\otimes m})\longrightarrow H^0(X_K,(M_K)^{\otimes m})$$ is injective, where $X_K=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $M_K$ is the restricted module. For every closed point $x$ of $X_k$, both $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and the free rank-one module $(M^{\otimes m})_x$ have depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-depth]. The assertion includes $m=0$, with $M^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_X$. No smoothness or normality of $X$, no nodal hypothesis, and no properness assumption are required.

source.place: Agent extraction of original lattice proof steps 1--2, using algebra.tex Tag 0337 (lemma-apply-grothendieck) and algebra.tex lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor; schemes.tex lemma-local-ring-fibre and morphisms.tex lemma-finite-type-noetherian supply the geometric local rings and Noetherian hypotheses. The reduced pure one-dimensional special-fibre condition is used only for the boundary-depth conclusion; flatness gives uniformizer torsion-freeness and generic restriction injectivity.

proof.text: Every ideal of $R$ is principal, so every ascending chain of ideals stabilizes: its union is generated by one element, which already lies in one member of the chain. Thus $R$ is Noetherian. Its spectrum is quasi-compact (the single affine chart suffices), hence Noetherian. Apply the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem to $f$. This proves that $X$ has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings. On any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ the ring $A$ is Noetherian; its localizations are Noetherian and are the local rings of $X$.

Fix $m\geq0$. A local generator $e$ of $M$ gives a generator $e^{\otimes m}$ of $M^{\otimes m}$, with $1$ as generator when $m=0$. Thus every stalk of this tensor power is free of rank one. At a point over the closed point of $S$, flatness says that $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a flat $R$-module. Since $R$ is a domain and $\pi\neq0$, the flat-module torsion-freeness lemma makes multiplication by $\pi$ injective there. At a point over the generic point, $\pi$ is a unit in the base field and therefore in the stalk. The same injectivity holds on the free rank-one stalk of $M^{\otimes m}$. These are all points: every nonzero element of $R$ is a unit times a power of $\pi$, so its only primes are $(0)$ and $(\pi)$.

source.place: Tag 0EX8 (lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring), general-case proof: torsion-freeness by flatness; algebra.tex Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr)

proof.text: Let $s$ be a section of $M^{\otimes m}$ restricting to zero on $X_K$. Cover $X$ by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ on which $M$ is free, and write $s|_U=a e^{\otimes m}$. The affine generic-fibre comparison identifies the restriction of $a$ to $U_K$ with $a/1\in A[1/\pi]$; hence it is zero. Here $\pi$ denotes its image in $A$. It is a nonzerodivisor in $A$: if $\pi b=0$, step 2 gives zero for every germ of $b$, so the sheaf axiom gives $b=0$. The nonzerodivisor-localization lemma now yields $a=0$. Consequently $s|_U=0$ on the cover, and the sheaf axiom gives $s=0$. Pullback of the chosen generator identifies $(M^{\otimes m})|_{X_K}$ with $(M_K)^{\otimes m}$, including the unit generator for $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 055J (lemma-connected-flat-over-dvr), affine generic-fibre localization calculation; divisors.tex Tag 07ZU, nonzerodivisor localization calculation

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x\in X_k$, and put $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{X_k,x}$. The fibre-stalk quotient theorem identifies $B=A_x/\pi A_x$. It is Noetherian, since ideals of a quotient lift to ideals of $A_x$, and it is reduced by the reduced-scheme definition. The morphism $X_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by base change. Apply the equidimensional-open local-dimension lemma with $O=X_k$ and $n=1$: the topological local dimension at $x$ is one. Choose an affine finite-type $k$-chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$ containing $x$ from the definition of locally finite type. Since $x$ is closed, its prime $\mathfrak n$ in $C$ is maximal. Open neighbourhoods inside $V$ are cofinal among neighbourhoods of $x$, so the local dimension in $V$ is also one. The closed-point dimension theorem and the affine-stalk localization identify $\dim B=\dim C_{\mathfrak n}=1$. In particular the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ is nonzero.

The maximal ideal of $B$ is not an associated prime of the $B$-module $B$. Indeed, suppose $\operatorname{ann}(b)=\mathfrak m_B$. If $b$ is a unit, its annihilator is zero, contradicting $\mathfrak m_B\neq0$. Otherwise $b\in\mathfrak m_B$, whence $b^2=0$. Reducedness gives $b=0$, whose annihilator is $B$, not its proper maximal ideal. The nonzerodivisor lemma therefore supplies $t\in\mathfrak m_B$ with multiplication by $t$ injective on $B$. Since $t$ is not a unit, $B/tB\neq0$, so $(t)$ is a regular sequence and $\operatorname{depth}(B)\geq1$.

The sequence $(\pi)$ is regular on $R$: $R$ is a domain, $\pi\neq0$, and $R/\pi R=k\neq0$. Thus $\operatorname{depth}(R)\geq1$. The stalk homomorphism $R\to A_x$ is flat and local by the definition of the flat scheme morphism; both rings are Noetherian by step 1, and its closed fibre is $B$ by step 4. The flat local depth formula gives $\operatorname{depth}(A_x)=\operatorname{depth}(R)+\operatorname{depth}(B)\geq2$. Finally a free rank-one identification $(M^{\otimes m})_x\cong A_x$ preserves multiplication, its successive quotients, and their nonvanishing. It therefore identifies the regular sequences and their suprema defining depth. This proves depth at least two for the module as well, for every $m$, including $m=0$.

No new nodes were added. Live and side-live still show the item as unsplit, so no other group superseded it, and there is no re-split note. Step-by-step checks: R is Noetherian because its ideals are principal; X is Noetherian by 01T6, and affine opens and localizations stay Noetherian (00FN). Stalks are π-torsion-free by flatness and the torsion-free-domain leaf, and primes of R are (0) or (π) by the unit-times-power node. Generic restriction is injective by the 055J affine model ε(i*a)=a/1, π being a nonzerodivisor on A, and localization injectivity. The special-fibre stalk is A_x/πA_x by 0HA1. Pure dimension one with 0A21 gives dim_x X_k=1, and 00OU at the closed point gives dim B=1, so m_B is nonzero. The reduced-ring annihilator argument and 00LL give a B-regular element, and 0337 (algebra.tex:46374) gives depth A_x=depth R+depth B>=2. Small cases behave as stated: R[t] (the generic point of the fibre has depth 1, so restricting to closed points is right), Spec R (fibre dimension 0), the nodal fibre uv=π (depth 2) and R[u,v]/(u^2,uv) (reducedness is needed). Batch-5 finding: lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain is a Mathlib leaf stating plain commutative algebra (flat over a domain implies torsion-free, More on Algebra 0539/053E). It is not part of either assumed statement or their proofs, so I accepted it. There is no SGA citation, and proof_deps equal the union of the step uses. Maintainer note: lem-sfb-trait-line-section-generic-germs-extension (Q136, unsplit) overlaps the injectivity and depth clauses and should cite this item when it is split.
